text:
Twenty-two headless Isaac flights of the whole mission today, beside four U-push flights from 11-03. They used the v21 valve with the hub pad's measured 72 mN·m. Unless a row says otherwise, each flight used the shipped approach: the claw follows the vehicle down, settles, and is then held in the room for the turn. The arm GS flew every step. A "drift seed" adds the slow random force that reproduced the hardware's hover wander on 10-21. The U-push rows are the 11-03 configuration on the same plant.

  • The plate push completes as reliably as the U push. Every unforced room-held plate flight completed: nine of nine at two poses, nominal, drift seeds 2, 3 and 4, and an aim 12 mm off the fin's radius. The valve turned 91–101°, the tilt stayed at or below 3.7° and DIRECT was never lost. The U push also completed every one of its conditions in Isaac.
  • When the plate push goes wrong, it aborts cleanly. Aimed 30 mm toward the plate's edge, the across guard stopped it with the outer tip 7 mm from the edge. Aimed 20 mm high, the depth guard stopped it before the turn. With no slack, the nose pushed the valve 15° in the hold and the station aborted when the hand-over did not settle. Every abort kept DIRECT with the tilt at or below 3.8°. So keep the 20 mm slack and aim on the fin's radius.
  • It needs the room hold. With the claw following the vehicle through the turn, one flight in four completed. The vehicle's wander went straight into the valve: one turned it 107°, then the nose fell 61 mm behind the plate.
  • The pose: keep [0, 5, 25, 0]°. Both [0, 5, 25, 0]° and [0, 0, 30, 0]° completed every flight. Under drift, q3 peaked in the turn at 31.8–34.5° at [0, 5, 25, 0], but at 37.2–39.2° at [0, 0, 30, 0], within 0.8° of the fin guard's 40° jam limit. [0, −5, 35, 0]° starts at q3 = 35° and tripped that limit after 14° of valve turn.
  • Coming down from above works. With Side Margin 0, the claw descends straight onto its hold instead of sliding toward the plate. Two of three such flights completed. The third aborted before the turn with nothing touching: the hover's sideways wander left the claw 37 mm off the plate's centreline, past the 35 mm across limit. Before the turn that error peaked at 6–37 mm across the eight drift flights, so the limit trips about once in eight.
  • Before the turn the plate is pushed far less. Under drift the nose came within 1 mm of the face in four of eight flights, yet the valve moved at most 0.4°. The U push's bracket moved it 0.3–5.1° in the same conditions.
  • Yaw and the landing gear. In the hold before Ready the yaw command already averages 0.125 N·m in every run, the simulated plant's standing load. The turn raises its 95th percentile by about 0.06 N·m with the plate and by 0.05–0.12 N·m with the U push. The larger change is height. The closed claw pushes with its tip, while the U pushed with its bracket 54 mm up the claw, so the vehicle flies about 46 mm higher. The landing gear and the arm then stay 54–72 mm from the nearest marker ball, against 10–16 mm for the U push.
note:
What these flights cannot show. Isaac never jammed the fin in the U. The U push completed every run here, including the 11-03 situation (no slack and 12 mm off), and Isaac's slide-in does not overshoot the way the hardware's did on 11-03 (18 mm): nominal flights ended Ready within 2 mm of the planned 20 mm gap. So the simulation cannot show that the plate, or coming down from above, prevents the 11-03 failure. The plate prevents it by its shape. No part of the fin is ever inside the claw, and a nose on a flat face can only be pushed sideways as hard as friction allows. Isaac shows the rest: the plate push works, aborts cleanly when it goes wrong, pushes the valve less before the turn, and gives the gear more room.

Reading the table.

  • Peak tilt runs from DIRECT entry and lowest q3 from Ready, both to the end of the run. Highest q3 covers the turn only, the window of the 40° jam limit.
  • Yaw command is the law's yaw torque in the turn. Sideways force is the controller's own estimate of the force on the claw across the vehicle, low-passed 0.5 s.
  • Nose on the plate is where the claw touched the plate in the turn: out from the shaft and up from the table. The plate spans 100–220 and 125–204 mm.
  • Before the turn gives the pushing point's closest approach to the face it pushes, from Ready's end, and how far the valve moved. The slack is 20 mm for the plate and 13 mm for the U push.
  • The abort reasons are the planner's guards, renamed here for the plate. The planner's own messages still say "fin" and "bracket".

With the 97° plan the valve ended 1–11° past 90°. The free-axis anchor lets the valve follow the vehicle's lead along the push. For a nominal end at 90°, plan about 95°.
